title: Publicly-Stated Hybrid Models for Remote Work - large tech firms
html:
Over the past few months, many of the largest technology firms have publicly announced, at least parts of, their policies related to remote and hybrid work arrangements as a result of the COVID pandemic. Understandably, each announcement produced its own series of news articles and never resulted in an overall comparison of the approaches that these companies were planning to take.

As part of her ongoing research regarding (completely) Remote Teams who support humanitarian response both during and outside disasters, Sariel Lei came across many articles and announcements related to hybrid models.

Rather than letting this information simply pass us by, we have compiled it into a simple matrix so that we can easily gain a basic oversight and comparison of what the major technology firms are planning for their hybrid modes.

We hope that this matrix will give people a better overview of what large technology firms see as possible/appropriate and perhaps guide you in deciding what is best for your digitally-enable teams.

[PDF]

Note that this matrix looks at Hybrid models and thus excludes companies who were (or have become) completely remote organizations.

Andrej
teaser: A comparison of the remote and hybrid work policies large technology firms announced during the COVID pandemic.
seo_description: Sariel Lei's overview of publicly stated hybrid work models from large tech firms, from her research on remote teams supporting humanitarian response.
